# Independent audit: multi-input coupling and directional surplus

Audited the full source
`candidate 4bb4c167681e8955`.
Result: PASS. No mathematical repair identified. This does not establish
an anchor-selection theorem or unrestricted OC.

## 1. Conditional maps for merely convex bodies

The argument does not assume cross-coordinate differentiability. Over an
interior prefix, every remaining-coordinate fiber is full dimensional in
its remaining space, so W_i>0. Brunn--Minkowski applied to actual section
inclusions gives concavity of W_i^(1/(d-i)), hence its continuity on the
open projection. The interval endpoints are finite convex/concave
functions on the open prefix projection and are continuous there.

The truncated numerator in C_i has dimension d-i+1. Its corresponding
volume root is concave in (prefix,threshold): convex combinations of two
truncated conditional bodies lie in the intermediate truncated body.
Its positive domain s>l_i(prefix) is open and convex. Thus the asserted
joint continuity on the proper interval is valid. At i=d the formula is
simply conditional interval length with W_d=1.

The inverse maps are continuous by local strict-monotonicity bracketing.
Their own derivatives are positive and continuous; their product telescopes
pointwise to |K|. A weighted sum of these maps is still triangular and
strictly increasing in the first differing coordinate. Its endpoint
functions are continuous in the source prefix, and after composing with
the already inverted prefix they are continuous in the image prefix.
This gives the claimed open recursive image and homeomorphism.

Repeated one-dimensional substitution is legitimate without any full
Jacobian theorem. For fixed prefixes the maps are C1 on an open interval;
apply ordinary substitution first on compact subintervals and then
monotone convergence for nonnegative integrands. Tonelli iterates these
identities. Possible endpoint derivative blow-up is harmless. The product
of own derivatives, not an unproved differentiable matrix determinant,
is the quantity used throughout.

## 2. Density and normalization

With b=sum lambda_j v_j^(1/d) and q_j=lambda_j v_j^(1/d)/b, weighted
AM--GM gives

    product_i sum_j lambda_j s_ji
      >=b^d product_j [product_i(s_ji/v_j^(1/d))]^q_j=b^d.

This uses the same cube point in every factor. Formula(4) then proves
rho=1/J_F composed with the inverse is the actual output density, with
integral one and bound1/B_lambda. The support is in the compact actual
Minkowski combination. The mean is the lambda-weighted mean of the
uniform input centroids. All these facts are simultaneous for every
subsequently chosen halfspace. Homothetic bodies attain the ceiling.
No smoothing, volume rescaling, or random choice of the eventual center
is hidden in the construction.

## 3. Source costs and every closed cap

The exact marginal source cost of an edge is t_E at EACH endpoint,
independent of its lambda weight. Thus the coefficient c_z in(7), and
not a lambda-discounted coefficient, is correct. For each sample an
output margin is a positive weighted average of source margins; if the
closed output cap contains it, at least one closed source cap contains
its source. This proves I_out<=N also on boundary samples.

Expanding(10), eta cancels with the negative I_out term in Delta, and
each endpoint contributes exactly t_E/v_z times its captured volume.
The remaining coefficient is1-c_z>=0. This proves the identity including
overlapping edges and own-fiber reuse, all oblique normals, and pure
integer caps. There is no infimum interchange. Inequality(11) follows
pointwise from k-1>=k(k-1)/r for1<=k<=r; the k=0 case also holds.

The output moment is lambda-weighted, whereas the charged source moments
are unweighted. The source explicitly retains this distinction. Any
positive barycenter supported in K_p is in K_p; positive own-volume
weight places it in the interior. This membership fact alone supplies
no depth estimate. The d=0 counting statement invokes only the indicator
and budget identities, not a nonexistent exponent1/d. Nonparallel
intrinsic fibers are correctly outside the transport theorem.

## 4. Ordered pair geometry and the seven-fiber certificate

The paired-centroid-tail theorem is an explicitly identified archived
dependency. Reading that source confirms the stated coefficient2Gamma_d
and all shifts, including d=1; no stronger arbitrary-point pairing is
used. If u dot w>=0, each common pair threshold u dot(g_1-g_j) is
nonpositive, so every pair pays2Gamma_d b_j. The contained B_1 gives
Gamma_d b_1 in the anchor fiber. If u dot w<=0, the anchor cap contains
g_0 and paysGamma_d k, and pair1 still pays2Gamma_d b_1. These are the
two bounds whose minimum appears in(14). The collinear ordering is a
real geometric hypothesis and is not inferred from compatibility.

For a pure integer through-anchor cap, at least one full member of every
reflected pair and the full own fiber are captured. k+sum b_j dominates
both required lower bounds after using Gamma_d<=1/2. A parallel move of
any containing halfspace through Y only decreases its captured mass.

In the actual seven-fiber triangle family, k=1, sum b_j=7/8, b_1=9/16,
so the two coefficients are17/8 and37/16. Their minimum times4/9 is
17/18. M=11/4 has OC target11/18, giving exact surplus1/3. The chosen
point P/4 belongs to the anchor through actual containment. Binary padding
leaves that block's all-normal lower bound unchanged while multiplying
both total mass and the arithmetic denominator by2^(n-1). The proof does
not say17/18 is exact depth or refute the older scalar-envelope obstruction.
It uses precisely the component shape and centroid-order data that the
older envelope omitted.

The multi-input theorem is useful beyond pairs, but the source correctly
does not attribute the seven-fiber improvement to multi-input coupling:
there only the paired-tail geometry is needed.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
